Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5 SMT solver, branch lazy).
Goal: in src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp, replace the per-lambda incremental
subsolver with enumeration in the MAIN solver: fresh integer skolems y for the lambda's bound
variables, a boolean guard skolem h (decision variable, phase-preferred true), lemmas
h => base(y) and h => not(D_i(y)) sent via TheoryArith's InferenceManager, the next cell read
from the main solver's candidate arithmetic model, and completeness detected when h is forced
false at decision level 0. Answer the specific questions for your assigned area with exact
signatures and file:line references. Return raw facts, not prose essays.
Area: src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_proof_generator.{h,cpp}. Questions:
1. List all register* methods with signatures and which proof rule each produces.
2. What happens if a lemma is sent with this generator but was never registered (getProofFor behavior)?
3. Is there a generic trust/assume fallback suitable for new lemma kinds (h => base(y), h => not(D(y))),
   or is passing nullptr as the generator the safer route when proofs are enabled?

facts: LiaStarProofGenerator lives at /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_proof_generator.h (164 lines) and .cpp (144 lines); class declared at liastar_proof_generator.h:60 as `class LiaStarProofGenerator : protected EnvObj, public ProofGenerator`.

There are exactly four register* methods, each storing the lemma in two user-context CDHashMaps (d_kind: Node->uint32_t at .h:152, d_aux: Node->Node at .h:154) keyed by the exact lemma node; constructor `LiaStarProofGenerator(Env& env, context::Context* c)` (.h:63, .cpp:31) and it is instantiated with env.getUserContext() in liastar_extension.cpp:270, gated by env.isTheoryProofProducing() (liastar_extension.cpp:268).
registerSplit (.h:71, .cpp:36) -> getProofFor builds via mkSplitProof (.cpp:88-95): a real (non-trust) ProofRule::SPLIT step `cdp.addStep(lemma, ProofRule::SPLIT, {}, {vp})` proving `vp OR (not vp)`.

registerNonnegative (.h:79, .cpp:42) -> mkNonnegativeProof (.cpp:97-110): trusted step `cdp.addTrustedStep(lemma, TrustId::ARITH_LIA_STAR_NONNEGATIVE, {literal}, {})` -- note it has the STAR_CONTAINS literal as a PREMISE (open assumption), so the resulting proof is not closed by itself.

registerContainsReduce (.h:88, .cpp:48) -> mkContainsReduceProof (.cpp:112-122): trusted step `cdp.addTrustedStep(lemma, TrustId::ARITH_LIA_STAR_CONTAINS_REDUCE, {}, {})` with no premises (the `star` param is ignored; recoverable as lemma[1]).

registerGuardDeactivate (.h:97, .cpp:57) -> mkGuardDeactivateProof (.cpp:124-132): trusted step `cdp.addTrustedStep(lemma, TrustId::ARITH_LIA_STAR_GUARD_DEACTIVATE, {}, {})`, no premises; d_aux is set to the lemma itself and unused. This is the existing 'fresh boolean guard fixed to false' pattern -- directly the shape needed for the planned `not h` completeness lemma.

The three lia* TrustIds are declared in /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/src/proof/trust_id.h:178 (ARITH_LIA_STAR_NONNEGATIVE), :184 (ARITH_LIA_STAR_CONTAINS_REDUCE), :191 (ARITH_LIA_STAR_GUARD_DEACTIVATE), with toString cases in trust_id.cpp:98-103.

Q2 (unregistered fact): hasProofFor(fact) (.cpp:63-66) returns false if the fact is not in d_kind. getProofFor(fact) (.cpp:68-86) does `Assert(it != d_kind.end())` at .cpp:71-72; with CVC5_ASSERTIONS this is AlwaysAssert (base/check.h:121-122) and throws/aborts with message 'LiaStarProofGenerator::getProofFor: unknown fact'. In a non-assertions (production) build the Assert is compiled out and the code dereferences the end() iterator of the CDHashMap (`(*it).second` at .cpp:74 and `(*auxIt).second` at .cpp:77) -- undefined behavior; if the garbage kind value misses the switch it hits Unreachable() at .cpp:85, which is CVC5_FATAL and always enabled (base/check.h:190). There is NO graceful fallback (no nullptr return, no generic trust step) for unregistered facts.

Q3 (fallback): there is no generic trust/assume register method in this generator -- every lemma must be registered under one of the four enum Kinds (.h:106-112). However, passing pg=nullptr is fully safe when proofs are enabled: InferenceManagerBuffered::addPendingLemma already defaults pg to nullptr (signature `bool addPendingLemma(Node lem, InferenceId id, LemmaProperty p = LemmaProperty::NONE, ProofGenerator* pg = nullptr, bool checkCache = true)` at /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/src/theory/inference_manager_buffered.h:64-68), and TheoryEngine::lemma handles generator-less trust nodes at /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/src/theory/theory_engine.cpp:1641-1652 by adding `d_lazyProof->addTrustedStep(lemma, TrustId::THEORY_LEMMA, {}, {tidn})` (tidn = THEORY_ARITH id node). So nullptr degrades to a coarse THEORY_LEMMA trust step instead of crashing.

Existing call sites pass d_proofGen.get() (which is already nullptr when proofs are disabled) to d_im.addPendingLemma: liastar_extension.cpp:344-345 (nonnegative, InferenceId::ARITH_LIA_STAR_NONNEGATIVE), :354-355 (split, ARITH_LIA_STAR_SPLIT), :452-453 and :927-928 (reduction, ARITH_LIA_STAR_EXISTS), :885-886 (guard deactivate, ARITH_LIA_STAR_SPLIT), :915-916 (guard split, ARITH_LIA_STAR_SPLIT); each is guarded by `if (d_proofGen != nullptr) d_proofGen->register...` (e.g. :340-343, :881-884, :923-926).

Recommendation derived from the code: for the new enumeration lemmas `h => base(y)` and `h => not(D_i(y))`, either (a) pass nullptr as the generator (safe, yields TrustId::THEORY_LEMMA via theory_engine.cpp:1649), or (b) follow the registerGuardDeactivate pattern: add a new Kind enum value, a registerX(Node lemma) method, a TrustId in proof/trust_id.{h,cpp}, and a one-line mkXProof emitting addTrustedStep with no premises. Do NOT send a lemma with d_proofGen.get() without registering it first -- that is the one combination that breaks (Q2). Note h => base(y) with fresh skolems y and fresh guard h is satisfiability-preserving (purely definitional/guarded), so a no-premise trust step in the style of mkGuardDeactivateProof is sound; reusing registerGuardDeactivate verbatim would 'work' mechanically (its proof ignores d_aux and trusts any lemma node) but would mislabel the step as ARITH_LIA_STAR_GUARD_DEACTIVATE.

caveats: mkNonnegativeProof produces a proof with the STAR_CONTAINS literal as an open premise of the trusted step (.cpp:107-108); any new lemma kind copying that pattern must ensure the premise is derivable in the surrounding LazyCDProof, otherwise the proof is not closed. The no-premise pattern (mkContainsReduceProof / mkGuardDeactivateProof) avoids this.

The maps are keyed on the exact Node sent: if the inference manager rewrites or caches the lemma differently from what was registered, getProofFor will be queried with a node that misses the map and trips the Assert (.cpp:71). Register exactly the node passed to addPendingLemma (this is what all current call sites do).

Maps live in the user context (liastar_extension.cpp:270 passes env.getUserContext()); registrations survive SAT-context push/pop but vanish on user-level pop -- fine for lemmas, which are user-context scoped.

The unregistered-fact behavior differs by build: assertion builds fail loudly via AlwaysAssert; production builds hit undefined behavior dereferencing CDHashMap::end() at .cpp:74/77 before any Unreachable() backstop. Treat 'generator passed but lemma not registered' as a hard bug in all builds.

d_proofGen is only allocated when env.isTheoryProofProducing() (liastar_extension.cpp:268-271), so d_proofGen.get() is itself nullptr in non-proof runs; the nullptr-generator path through theory_engine.cpp:1644-1652 is only exercised when proofs ARE enabled, and it succeeds (TrustId::THEORY_LEMMA), so nullptr is safe but gives the coarsest possible proof granularity.

I did not verify whether any proof postprocessor or --proof-granularity option rejects TrustId::THEORY_LEMMA steps for arith; if strict proof checking of trust steps is required downstream, the dedicated-TrustId route (option b) gives clearer provenance than nullptr.
